NO LAND_TEXTURES ROW YET — written out ready in the ISLAND_STYLES comment in script.js. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, at 1254px (downsampled to 1024 by ingest; mean and sd unchanged). ALPHA MEASURED TO 0.30, one step under the sward family's 0.40-0.50, because this is the busiest sward ever delivered — luma sd 19.17 at tile 128 against bay-scrub's 14.21, which was itself described as 'much busier than the two swards'. 0.40 would have landed on-screen sd 7.67, past `grass` (6.66) and the loudest ground in the game. 0.30 lands 5.75, effectively on top of bay-scrub's 5.68 and between swampgrass (5.07) and grass (6.66). Third sward running to come off its pre-registered value for exactly this reason (marsh 0.5->0.40, coastalscrub 0.5->0.40, this 0.40->0.30) — the pattern is now strong enough to state as a rule: pre-register a sward at 0.30 and measure up, not 0.50 and measure down. ⚠️ PERIODICITY WAS MEASURED TWO WAYS AND THE FIRST ONE NEARLY GOT THIS REJECTED. On the radially averaged power spectrum it scores peak/mean 20.34 at 4 cycles per tile — by far the worst in the set, whose shipped range is 8.65 (grass) to 12.18 (bay-scrub) — which reads as a clear fail. It is not one. peak/mean is normalised by the BROADBAND FLOOR, and this art has an unusually smooth one, so the ratio inflates without the repeat being any stronger. Measured in absolute on-screen terms instead — the luma sd carried by the dominant band, times alpha — it is 3.48 at 0.30, BELOW bay-scrub's 3.72 and marsh's 3.68, both shipped and accepted. JUDGE A REPEAT ON ABSOLUTE AMPLITUDE; the ratio misleads in both directions, and this is the second metric on this venue to do so (see the elongation-vs-direction note on bayou-oak). WRAP IS CLEAN: 1.11 horizontal and 0.87 vertical against interior, i.e. at or below the interior neighbour difference, and no seam visible in a 3x3 tiling. ⚠️ THE CROWN CONSTRAINT SURVIVED, BUT ONLY WHEN CHECKED PROPERLY, and this is the finding worth carrying to any future ground that grows trees. Delivered mean is #A9AF2A at L* 68.9, four L* darker than the #AABD31 spec. Checked against the SPEC HEX LADDER the note above lists, that looks like an outright failure: the ground is 5.3 L* DARKER than the palm's lit frond tone (#94C701, L* 74.3), and the note demands it be lighter than every crown tone. It is not a failure, because a lit tone is a HIGHLIGHT on a minority of a crown's pixels and is never what the crown reads as. Measured on the real sprites: the shipped lagoon palms average L* 47.8 and 46.8, so this ground sits +21.2 above them — in family with the cove, where bay-scrub at L* 66.3 sits +26.0 / +37.2 / +32.2 above its own three trees. COMPARE CROWN MEANS TO GROUND MEANS. A spec hex ladder is for writing a prompt, not for judging one. SATURATION CLEARED COMFORTABLY at 0.76 against the 0.60 reject line, so the drab failure this family keeps having did not recur. Separations on the delivered mean: in-venue 58.3 from `coralsand` and 57.2 from `coralrock`; cross-venue 14.0 from `coastalscrub`, 18.4 from `grass`, 30.7 from `swampgrass`, all picker-only. Body reset to the delivered mean; stroke/veg are the spec's offsets carried onto it, `rock` is the venue's own limestone. Registered `tropicscrub`, tile 128, alpha 0.30.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF THE TOP OF ONE SHRUB, shot straight down from well above it the way a survey frames a single plant. YOU SEE FOLIAGE AND NOTHING ELSE: no trunk, no stem, no limb, no branch, no twig and no bark anywhere in this picture, and least of all in the middle. Where the mass parts you see hard-edged SHADOW INSIDE THE PLANT, never a branch. BEACH NAUPAKA — Scaevola taccada, the shrub that lines every sand beach in the South Pacific, growing in the salt spray right down to the high-water mark. It is THE DENSE ONE of this venue's three ground plants, and its whole job is to be a solid mass: a compact, closed, ROUNDED MOUND of leaf, tight and heavy, with no gaps you can see the ground through. THE LEAF IS THICK, FLESHY AND GLOSSY, and that is what separates this from any ordinary bush. Build the mound from broad SPOON-SHAPED leaves — widest near the blunt rounded tip and tapering back to the stalk — each one a chunky two-tone shape with a hard edge and a bright specular sheen along one side, because these leaves are succulent and wet-looking. The leaves crowd into tight spiral clusters at the end of every branch, so the surface of the mound reads as a quilt of overlapping ROSETTES of six to ten leaves each, packed together at plainly uneven sizes. COUNT NOTHING AND REPEAT NOTHING. The rosettes clump and crowd; they do not sit in a ring around a centre and there is no rosette in the middle with the others arranged about it. Walk around the rim, and if the same cluster spacing comes back four, five or six times on the way round, it has been drawn as a FLOWER and it is wrong however good it looks. AND YET IT IS ONE COMPACT CONNECTED MOUND, which is the other half of that rule and the easier half to lose. Every cluster touches or overlaps a neighbour and NOT ONE floats off on its own with clear space round it. Draw the smallest circle that contains the plant and the foliage fills about eight tenths of it — this is the densest thing in the venue's planting and it should read as solid. The rim is lumpy and bitten, with two or three shallow notches, and it is never a clean circle. THE WHITE HALF-FLOWERS ARE THE IDENTIFIER AND THEY ARE THE POINT OF THE NAME. Naupaka means half-flower: the bloom looks as though it has been torn down the middle, with every petal on ONE side of the centre and nothing on the other — a small white fan of five petals in a half-circle, faintly streaked purple at the throat. Scatter six to ten of them unevenly across the mound, each small, each sitting in the middle of a leaf rosette, and a few small round white berries among them. They are the ONLY light accent in the picture and the only thing that is not green. THE GREEN IS A BRIGHT GLOSSY TROPICAL YELLOW-GREEN, HIGH IN CHROMA. Build the whole plant from this set: a bright lit green near #7FB82A on the leaves that catch the sun, a mid green near #4D8C15, a full-bodied green near #2F6A0E, and a deep COOL shade near #16400A in the pockets between clusters. THERE IS NO OLIVE, NO KHAKI, NO MUSTARD, NO OCHRE, NO TAN, NO ARMY DRAB AND NO DUSTY, GREYED-DOWN OR MUTED GREEN ANYWHERE IN THIS PLANT. Where it turns into shadow it goes deeper and cooler, never browner and never duller. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE. A mound seen from straight above is round; one wider than it is tall means the camera was tilted. NO WATER ANYWHERE: no waterline, no wet stain, no reflection. And no ground is DRAWN either — a sand beach is where it grows, not something painted into the sprite; the plant is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the shore it stands on
assets.note: FIRST OF BLUEWATER BONANZA'S THREE UNDERBRUSH PLANTS, and the venue's default coastal bush — the one that will be placed most, behind beaches and along every shoreline. The set is separated on SILHOUETTE FIRST per art-pipeline 2's colour-removed test: this is a DENSE CLOSED MOUND, [[ocean-morning-glory]] is an OPEN SPRAWL OF RUNNERS, and [[ocean-grass-coastal]] is a SOFT FEATHERED TUFT. Size ladder 40 / 30 / 20 — 1.33x and 1.50x apart, matching the cove shrub family's own minimum. SIZE IS HONEST, NOT EXAGGERATED: an open-grown Scaevola taccada spreads about 4.35 m, and 4.35 x 9.2 units/m = 40u. It sits just above the cove's largest shrub (cove-oak-scrub, 36u), which is right — a naupaka thicket is bigger than a bear oak. ⚠️ IT IS COLOUR-TWINNED WITH THE COCONUT PALM AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Measured, its body sits dE 3.6 from the shipped palm crown — effectively the same green. art-pipeline 2 asks that role and identity survive with COLOUR REMOVED, which is exactly the axis these two are separated on: 40u against 70u, and a closed lumpy mound against a rosette of long feathered blades. Both are also genuinely the same bright glossy yellow-green in life. Do not 'fix' this by tinting one of them; that would trade a real distinction for a fake one. Same argument covers [[ocean-morning-glory]] at dE 7.9 from the pandanus. READS DARK ON BOTH ITS GROUNDS, the constraint the whole venue's planting is built on: L* 52.3 against tropicscrub's 68.9 (+16.6) and coralsand's 90.9 (+38.6). That is within 0.3 L* of the shipped coconut palm's own relationship to the same grounds, so a beach planted with both reads as one family. THE HALF-FLOWER IS WORTH THE PIXELS AT 40u and is the reason this slot names a flower at all, where the cove's shrubs mostly do not. It is the species' name and its one unmistakable feature, it is WHITE against a saturated green so it survives reduction better than any hue would, and it is the only light accent in the venue's entire planting — nothing else here reads as a bright speck. planRound true, fillTo 0.86, anchor trunk-base with no trunk drawn (the cove-oak-black convention: the stem's position is implied at the mound's centre). NO allowSymmetry — a shrub built from leaf ROSETTES sits right on the mandala attractor, which is why the subject spends a clause refusing evenness and states the clump construction instead, the cove-pine-pitch lesson. Plane `surface` and contact none when the art lands: nothing sails under a bush, and it stands on tropicsand and tropicscrub, both already `hard`. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6: slot, then art, then the kind. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, pre-cut with real alpha, 2048px master, ingested with no warnings (160px bake for 40px display). EVERY GATE PASSED. Aspect 1.004 against the 1.12 planRound gate. One connected mound, no floating cluster. Circle fill 74.6% against the eight tenths asked — marginally under and correctly the densest thing in the venue's planting. Green-only hue 93 at saturation 0.81, so the bright glossy yellow-green arrived and the drab failure did not recur; 97.8% of opaque pixels are green and only 0.8% warm. THE HALF-FLOWERS AND BERRIES CAME THROUGH and they do the identifying work the note above predicted: white against a saturated green survives reduction where a hue would not, and at 40px they are the only bright specks in the whole venue's planting. READS AT ITS OWN SIZE ON BOTH GROUNDS, measured by compositing the 40px sprite over each: dE 27.3 from tropicscrub and 61.2 from coralsand, covering 59% of its own footprint. Body L* 50.2, so the scrub sits +18.7 above it and the sand +40.7 — in family with the shipped coconut palm's +16.4 / +38.4, which is what makes a beach planted with both read as one set. ROSETTE CHECK: strongest angular harmonic n=4 carrying 34.9%, a shade over the accepted cove oak's 33% and far under the rejected cove pine's 71%. Accepted — a shrub built from leaf rosettes has some angular structure by construction, and the bilateral test below confirms it is not a stamped mandala. No halo: the ordering test reads -0.28 luma mean at display size, so the pixels ship exactly as delivered. Registered `ocean-naupaka`, world 40, plane surface, contact none.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE LOW VINE SPRAWLING ACROSS BARE SAND, shot straight down from well above it. You are looking at a plant that lies FLAT ON THE GROUND — it has no height at all, so nothing here is seen from the side and nothing casts a shape but itself. BEACH MORNING GLORY — Ipomoea pes-caprae, the goat's-foot vine, the first plant to colonise an open beach and the one that holds the sand together. It is THE OPEN ONE of this venue's three ground plants, and its whole job is to soften bare sand WITHOUT adding bushy volume. THE RUNNERS ARE THE SUBJECT, AND THEY MUST READ AS LINES. From a single off-centre root, five to eight long stems run outward across the ground in different directions, each one a clean narrow line of reddish-green that stays about the same width for its whole length and never tapers away. They do not radiate evenly: two or three run much further than the rest, one or two bend and curve as they go, and one crosses over a neighbour. Along every runner, single rounded leaves are spaced out at intervals on short stalks, alternating from side to side, closer together near the root and further apart toward the tip. ⚠️ THE SPACE BETWEEN THE RUNNERS IS EMPTY AND IT IS MOST OF THE PICTURE. This is a net over the ground, not a mass: the transparent background shows through everywhere between the stems, in big open wedges, and the plant covers only about a third of the circle it reaches across. IF IT COMES BACK AS A SOLID ROUND CUSHION OF LEAVES IT IS WRONG — that is a bush, and this venue already has one. The only thing holding it together is the runners themselves meeting at the root. THE LEAF IS A GOAT'S FOOT, which is the species' name and its identifier at any size: a thick, glossy, almost circular leaf with a deep NOTCH cut into its outer tip, splitting it into two rounded lobes exactly like a cloven hoof print. Every leaf shows that notch. Twenty to thirty-five leaves in the whole plant, each one flat to the ground and drawn as one chunky two-tone shape with a hard edge. THE FLOWERS ARE THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT GREEN AND THEY CARRY THE PLANT AT SMALL SIZE. Three or four open trumpets, seen from DIRECTLY ABOVE so each is a flat round disc — a shallow five-lobed pinwheel with faint radiating seams and a small paler star at the centre where the throat goes down. A deep orchid magenta near #BD3995, with the throat a paler warm pink. NOT a hot fluorescent pink, not red, not purple-blue: a rich saturated pink-magenta. Set them on the runners, never at the root, and never all on one side. A couple of unopened buds, tight furled cones of the same colour, among them. THE GREEN IS A DEEP GLOSSY SEA-BEACH GREEN. Build the leaves from this set: a lit green near #3FA83F on the leaves that catch the sun, a mid green near #17751B, a full-bodied green near #0C5416, and a deep cool shade near #04310F where a leaf overlaps a runner. The runners themselves are a shade warmer and redder than the leaves. NO OLIVE, NO KHAKI, NO MUSTARD, NO TAN, NO ARMY DRAB AND NO DUSTY OR GREYED-DOWN GREEN. TAKEN AS A WHOLE THE PLANT REACHES AS FAR UP AS IT DOES ACROSS — the runners go out in all directions, so the overall spread is roughly as tall as it is wide, even though the plant itself is mostly empty space. It must not become a one-sided fan or a streak running off in a single direction. NO WATER ANYWHERE, and NO SAND IS DRAWN either even though sand is where it grows — the vine is alone on a transparent background and the engine supplies the beach under it. No shadow, no footprints, no shells, no driftwood
assets.note: THE VENUE'S GROUNDCOVER, and the answer to a real gap: palm, pandanus, almond and naupaka are all MASSES, so a cay planted only with those is a set of blobs on blank sand. This is the one that softens open sand without adding another blob. See [[ocean-naupaka]] for the family's size ladder and shared reasoning. SIZE IS HONEST AND CONSERVATIVE: 30u = 3.26 m across. A real Ipomoea pes-caprae runner goes 10 m and more, so if anything this under-sells it; 30 was chosen to sit a clean 1.33x under the naupaka rather than to match the plant. ⚠️ THIS IS THE ONE ASSET IN THE VENUE THAT MUST FAIL THE COMPACTNESS TEST, and that has to be written down before delivery or it will be rejected by a check that does not apply. [[ocean-naupaka]] asks for eight tenths of its enclosing circle and the trees ask for seven; this asks for about ONE THIRD, because the open sand between the runners IS the asset. [[ocean-pandanus]] already came in at 52% against a 70% ask and was accepted on the same reasoning — a subject whose gaps are the point cannot be judged by fill. The invariant that DOES apply here is connectedness: every runner must meet at the root, so one connected piece, no leaf drifting free. Check that, and check the overall reach is roughly as tall as it is wide; ignore fill entirely. MAGENTA IS INFORMATION, NOT DECORATION, which is what earns it under art-pipeline 3c — colour that carries information wins even where it appears nowhere else in the venue, and this flower appears nowhere else by a wide margin: measured, #BD3995 sits dE 87-128 from every green in the venue's planting. At 30u the leaves are 3-4 px each and the flowers are most of what a player actually resolves, so they are doing the identification work. The subject deliberately says orchid-magenta and refuses HOT pink, because the prop venue clause names neon and hot pink as alien hues and a prompt that asks for one while the clause refuses it is the self-contradiction this pipeline has paid for twice. READS DARK ON BOTH GROUNDS: L* 42.7, so tropicscrub sits +26.2 above it and coralsand +48.2 — the strongest separation of the three underbrush, which it needs, being the most open. Colour-twinned with the pandanus at dE 7.9; separated on size (30 vs 52) and on silhouette (an open net against spiky rosettes), per [[ocean-naupaka]]'s note on the same situation with the palm. planRound true — the RUNNERS reach equally in all directions even though the plant is mostly empty, so the bbox test still catches a tilted camera. fillTo 0.86, anchor trunk-base at the root. NO allowSymmetry: evenly radiating runners would read as a starfish. Plane `surface`, contact none, when the art lands. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, pre-cut with real alpha, 2048px master, ingested with no warnings (120px bake for 30px display). THE OPEN-NET CONSTRUCTION ARRIVED EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED — runners radiating from an off-centre root, unevenly, some crossing, with round notched goat's-foot leaves spaced along them, three open magenta trumpets and three furled buds. Aspect 1.003. ⚠️ CIRCLE FILL 21.4%, AND THAT IS THE ASSET WORKING, NOT FAILING. The note above warned that a check written for compact crowns would reject this; the delivery came back more open still. The invariant that DOES apply was checked and holds: ONE connected piece, every runner meeting at the root, no leaf drifting free. It is also the least self-similar sprite in the venue by a wide margin — bilateral correlation 0.127 against the shipped cove oak's 0.696 — which is exactly right for an irregular sprawl and the strongest evidence the openness is real rather than a symmetric starfish. MAGENTA IS 10.8% OF THE OPAQUE PIXELS and is what carries the plant at size. At 30px the leaves are a few pixels each; measured over the scrub the whole plant reads dE 29.7 from its ground while covering only 29% of its footprint, so most of what a player resolves is the flowers. That is the art-pipeline 3c argument paying off — information-carrying colour doing the identification. Body L* 39.3: scrub +29.6, sand +51.6, the strongest separation of the three underbrush, which the most open one needs. Angular harmonic n=5 at 15.3%, the lowest of the set. No halo (-0.21 luma at display size). Registered `ocean-morning-glory`, world 30, plane surface, contact none.

assets.subject: THE PICTURE IS A DRONE PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE SMALL CLUMP OF COASTAL GRASS, shot straight down from well above it. Nothing of any side is visible: you see the top of the clump and nothing else. SALT-TOLERANT BEACH GRASS — the fine wiry bunchgrass of a windswept back-beach and a low sandy islet, sun-cured and dry. It is THE SOFT ONE of this venue's three ground plants, and it exists to break up open ground and make the place feel breezy, dry and exposed. IT IS A TUSSOCK, AND ITS OUTLINE IS SOFT AND FEATHERED — this is the single most important thing about the drawing, because there is another plant in this venue it must never be confused with. Its blades are FINE, NUMEROUS AND HAIR-LIKE: many thin threads springing from a tight base, arching outward and DROOPING so their tips bend over and down, giving a rim that is soft, wispy and broken. It is NOT a star, NOT a spiky rosette, and NOT built from a few chunky straps with hard edges and sharp points — that is a screw pine and it is the wrong plant. Where a strap plant has ten stiff blades, this has fifty fine ones. TWO OR THREE TUSSOCKS, NOT ONE, at plainly different sizes and merged where they touch, so the clump reads as a patch of grass rather than a single specimen. One obviously the largest, the others crowding it off to one side. They form ONE connected patch: no tussock floats off on its own. IT IS SUN-CURED, AND THAT IS ITS COLOUR. Most of every blade is a dry STRAW GOLD, warm and clean: a lit tone near #E0BC7C on the tips that catch the sun and a body near #D1A964 through the mass. Down at the base, where the clump is still alive and shaded, it goes GREEN — a mid green near #6E8A2E deepening to near #3A4A16 in the dark heart of the clump, so the patch reads gold at the rim and green at the middle. THAT TWO-TONE IS DELIBERATE AND MUST NOT BE FLATTENED: the gold is what makes this plant legible against green ground, and the green base is what keeps it from reading as dead straw. IT IS DRY, NOT DEAD, AND NOT DIRTY. Nothing here is grey, khaki, army drab, dusty, brown, rust or muddy. Cured grass in hard tropical sun is a warm clean gold, closer to wheat or straw than to earth; if a tone is in doubt push it toward YELLOW and toward LIGHT, never toward grey and never toward brown. TWO OR THREE FINE SEED SPIKES stand up out of the clump, each a slender straight stem with a narrow head of tiny grains, a shade darker than the blades. No more than three, and none of them longer than about a third of the clump's width — this is drawn very small and they are the first thing that will turn to mush. THE SILHOUETTE IS AS TALL AS IT IS WIDE and the clump is compact taken as a whole: draw the smallest circle that contains it and the grass fills about six tenths of it. Uneven at the rim, yes; drifting apart into a streak or a crescent, no. NO WATER ANYWHERE, and NO GROUND IS DRAWN — dry sand is where it grows, not something painted into the sprite. The clump is alone on a transparent background. No shadow, no soil, no shells, no flowers, no driftwood
assets.note: THE VENUE'S FILLER, for windy scrubby back-beach and low island interiors. Smallest asset Bluewater Bonanza has. See [[ocean-naupaka]] for the family's ladder and shared reasoning. ⚠️ SIZE IS EXAGGERATED AND THE MANIFEST'S SCALE BLOCK REQUIRES THAT TO BE DECLARED: a real coastal bunchgrass tussock is 0.6-1 m across, which is 6-9u and cannot carry a silhouette — the same argument the scale note makes for the penguin at 4.6px. 20u is about 2.2 m, so roughly a 2.5x exaggeration, and the subject compensates by asking for TWO OR THREE tussocks merged rather than one giant one, so what is drawn is an honest patch at an honest size rather than one implausible plant. ⚠️ THE ONLY PLANT IN THE VENUE THAT DOES NOT READ DARK, and the reason is measured. Every other planting here is a dark mass on a lighter ground — the trees run +16 to +37 L* below tropicscrub. A sun-cured grass is genuinely LIGHTER than the sward it stands in, so this one sits at L* 71.5 against the ground's 68.9: 2.5 L* ABOVE it, effectively equal. It therefore separates on HUE AND CHROMA INSTEAD, and that is what picked the colour. Swept against both its grounds, a straw gold at hue 38 lands dE 32.4 from tropicscrub and 35.7 from coralsand — comparable to the coconut palm's own 31.8 against the scrub — where the obvious yellow-green answer (hue 60-68, matching the ground's family) measured dE 6.4-13.3 and would have been invisible on the exact ground this asset exists to break up. IF A DELIVERY COMES BACK YELLOW-GREEN RATHER THAN GOLD, REJECT IT: it will disappear into the scrub, which is the one thing this slot cannot do. IT IS ALSO THE ONLY NON-GREEN VEGETATION IN THE VENUE, which is a bonus rather than the reason — it gives a planted interior a second colour without a second species. ⚠️ CONFUSABILITY WITH [[ocean-pandanus]] IS THE REAL RISK AND THE SUBJECT ATTACKS IT DIRECTLY. Both are radiating blade plants drawn from above, and the pandanus is itself 'two to six spiky rosettes clustered', which is structurally what a grass patch is. The separations: 20u against 52u (2.6x), gold against green (dE 54.7), and — the one that survives colour removal, which is what art-pipeline 2 actually requires — FINE SOFT FEATHERED blades that droop, against FEW STIFF CHUNKY straps with hard edges and points. The subject names the screw pine as the wrong answer explicitly, the bayou-moss method: state the geometry, give the correct read, then name the failure so a generator can refuse it. AT 20u THE DETAIL BUDGET IS ABOUT 20 SCREEN PIXELS, so the subject asks for the blade mass, the arch, the two-tone and at most three seed spikes, and nothing else. The cove's hydrangeas ship at 18u, so this size is proven, but they carry one flower head and no interior structure at all. Anything more here delivers mush. planRound true, fillTo 0.86, anchor trunk-base, no allowSymmetry. Plane `surface`, contact none, when the art lands. NOT REGISTERED IN PROP_KINDS YET, by art-pipeline 6. DELIVERED AND ACCEPTED 2026-08-14, pre-cut with real alpha, 2048px master, ingested with no warnings (80px bake for 20px display). Two merged tussocks with fine drooping blades, gold at the rim and green at the heart, three seed spikes — the whole construction as asked, and NOT a small pandanus: the blades are fine and feathered where a screw pine's are few and stiff. Aspect 1.024, one connected patch (99.95% in the largest component; the rest are blade tips detached by antialiasing). ⚠️ THE TWO-TONE IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORK AND IT ARRIVED: 68.9% of opaque pixels are warm straw and 27.2% are the green base. The gold is the majority tone, which is what the colour argument depended on. ⚠️ IT CAME BACK 12 L* DARKER THAN SPEC AND STILL PASSES — read this before 'correcting' it. The slot specified a mean of #D1A964 at L* 71.5, deliberately 2.5 L* ABOVE the scrub ground, on the reasoning that a cured grass is lighter than the sward it stands in. The delivery means #9D8A4E at L* 58.1, i.e. 10.8 BELOW the ground — apparently a miss on the one axis the slot cared about. It is not, because a raw mean is the wrong statistic for a finely feathered subject: most of this sprite's area is the dark air between hair-thin blades, which drags the mean down while contributing nothing to what a player sees. MEASURED THE WAY IT SHIPS — the 20px sprite composited over the ground it stands on — it reads dE 27.1 from tropicscrub and 32.3 from coralsand, against the naupaka's 27.3 and the swept target of ~32. The hue-not-value strategy holds intact. COMPOSITE AT DISPLAY SIZE BEFORE JUDGING ANY SPARSE SUBJECT'S COLOUR; the master's mean will lie to you in proportion to how much air it contains. ⚠️ ANGULAR HARMONIC n=2 AT 66.8%, WHICH LOOKS LIKE A REJECT AND IS NOT. It is close to the cove pine's rejected 71% and would fail the check as written. But n=2 is BILATERAL, not rotational — it is what any compact, roughly balanced blob scores, and it says nothing about the flower/rosette defect the metric exists to catch. Tested directly by mirroring the sprite onto itself: left-right correlation 0.592, against the SHIPPED AND ACCEPTED cove-oak-black at 0.696. The accepted art is more self-similar than this is. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN ONE SESSION AN ANGULAR METRIC HAS MISFIRED ON A SUBJECT IT WAS NOT WRITTEN FOR — the pandanus's n=3 was its head count, the almond's bullseye was invisible to it entirely (that needed a cap-offset test), and this n=2 is compactness. The rule that falls out: the polar spectrum only answers 'is this a ring of identical things around a hub'. For anything else, pick the test that matches the defect. No halo (+0.05 luma at display size, the cleanest of the three). Registered `ocean-grass-coastal`, world 20, plane surface, contact none.

scale.anchor: The player's boat. Hull is ~56 world units (see the repositionBoats comment in script.js) and the camera is 1:1, so 56px = one boat.
scale.boatLength: Treat the boat as a ~20ft (6.1m) sportboat. Nothing in the game names a class, so this is a free choice — and it is the one that makes the accepted art self-consistent. At J/105 scale (10.5m) everything already accepted would be ~2x oversize.
scale.note: Exaggeration is permitted and often required: a penguin's true overhead footprint is ~0.5m = 4.6px, which cannot carry a silhouette. Measured on arctic water, a 7-bird huddle needs ~70px before individual birds resolve and species colour appears. Exaggerate deliberately and record it here; do not drift.

pod.note: calf count decided once per pod; calves take the trailing indices

variance.source: hash(index, channel) — deterministic, never Math.random, so the render path cannot perturb the RNG stream the eval harness depends on

notes: surfaceDepth is deliberately NOT zero — a swimming orca is never fully out of the water, and bottoming the depth curve at 0 draws it flat on the surface like a decal.
The depth curve DWELLS: rise, swim up top, sink, stay down. A sine spends equal time everywhere and reads as bobbing.

Deep animals draw as a flat dark silhouette (#0a1a2c via source-atop), not as the faded real sprite. Losing the markings is what reads as UNDER water; a faded sprite reads as merely far away. Drone footage shows the opposite — markings persist at depth — but legibility at 40px beat accuracy here.

The blow is emitted in WORLD space at the animal's position when it blew, and stays put while the animal swims on. Evaluated analytically from past time, so there is no particle list and nothing to reset between races.
Blow density peaks at exhalation and only falls. Holding peak opacity while the sprite scales up reads as fading IN, which is a bug that took three passes to see.
Rejected after trying: bow wake, submerging foam, fluke prints as rings, and fluke prints as bubble scatters. All read as graphics rather than water.
